subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: When an operational notice cannot be written to the configured redirect session, should OpenClaw durably retain it for operator-only recovery, expose it to the source chat, or intentionally discard it?
rationale: Failing open can re-expose the sensitive operational details this feature is intended to contain, while the current fail-closed path loses the only notice; existing behavior does not establish which privacy-versus-availability contract maintainers intend.

options.title: Durable operator-only recovery
options.body: Suppress the source only after a durable operator-owned queue or equivalent recovery path accepts the notice for retry.

options.title: Fallback to source delivery
options.body: Deliver to the originating chat when redirect persistence fails, favoring immediate observability over confidentiality.

options.title: Accept explicit log-only loss
options.body: Keep the source silent and discard the notice, but document and surface that behavior through operator-visible diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Durable operator-only recovery
recommendation.body: Suppress the source only after a durable operator-owned queue or equivalent recovery path accepts the notice for retry.

likelyOwner.reason: His sampled history spans the core reply, session, plugin, and security-policy surfaces needed to choose this cross-boundary contract.
